scenario: AITA for telling my SIL to shut up? | My SIL drives me a little bonkers sometimes. She is extremely proud of things like not watching TV, not listening to pop music, not having Facebook, and she interrupts conversations to say it. Often insulting the thing as well, instead of just saying that she doesn’t like it. Instead it’s about her superiority for not liking it. A few days ago we were having dinner and my 14-year-old sister starts talking about she watched a Marvel movie and she’s looking forward to a sequel that should be coming out soon. My SIL said, “I’ve never watched any Marvel movies. They seem pretty awful.” I was pissed off, I don’t get why my SIL, an adult woman, feels the need to be so rude and dismissive towards a teenager. I said loudly, “shut up, not everything has to be about you and what you like.” She blushed and didn’t say anything more, my brother didn’t say anything either. But he messaged me after they left saying that this was my expression of “always hating” his wife and that I’m a bad person who doesn’t want her to participate in conversation. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my SIL (sister-in-law) to shut up during dinner. Let me start by understanding the situation better. My SIL is someone who is really proud of not watching TV, not listening to pop music, and not having Facebook. She often interrupts conversations to mention these things, and instead of just saying she doesn't like them, she makes it about her superiority for not liking them. A few days ago, during dinner, my 14-year-old sister started talking about a Marvel movie she watched and was looking forward to the sequel. My SIL interrupted and said she had never watched any Marvel movies and that they seemed pretty awful. I got really upset because I don't understand why my SIL feels the need to be so rude and dismissive towards a teenager. I told her loudly to shut up, saying that not everything has to be about her and what she likes. She blushed and didn't say anything more, and my brother didn't say anything either. But later, he messaged me saying that this was my expression of always hating his wife and that I'm a bad person who doesn't want her to participate in conversations. So, the question is: Is it right or wrong for me to tell my SIL to shut up in this situation? And why? First, I need to consider the context. My SIL's behavior seems to be consistently interrupting and making others feel bad about their interests. She's not just expressing her preferences but doing so in a way that's dismissive and superior. That's probably why I got upset when she interrupted my sister, especially since my sister is a teenager who's just sharing something she enjoys. On the other hand, telling someone to shut up, especially in front of others, can be seen as rude and aggressive. It might escalate the situation rather than resolving it. My brother's reaction, where he felt that I was expressing dislike for his wife and being a bad person, shows that my action had unintended consequences. I also need to think about the dynamics of the family. My brother is married to my SIL, so he might be more protective of her, which could explain his reaction. It's possible that he felt I was being unfair or harsh, even if my intentions were to stand up for my sister. Another angle is to consider alternative ways to handle the situation. Instead of telling her to shut up, maybe I could have addressed her behavior more calmly or found a way to redirect the conversation. That might have been more effective in resolving the conflict without making things worse. Additionally, I should reflect on my own feelings. Why did I get so upset? Was it because I felt my sister was being disrespected, or was there something else? Understanding my own emotions can help me address the situation more constructively in the future. In summary, while my intention was to stand up for my sister and address my SIL's dismissive behavior, the way I did it might have been seen as wrong because it was confrontational and led to negative consequences. It might have been better to handle the situation more calmly and find a constructive way to address the issue without escalating tensions.
